source: University Animal Hospital Zurich primary clinical-study pages

upsert.title: Oral vinorelbine Phase I for dogs with tumors
upsert.summary: Early Phase I study determining a safe oral dose of vinorelbine in dogs with cancer. Dogs may qualify when standard treatment is no longer appropriate or feasible; good general condition and body weight over 5 kg are required. Treatment includes a single oral vinorelbine dose after staging/screening.

upsert.title: ADAM-12 vaccine immunotherapy for feline soft tissue sarcoma
upsert.summary: Phase 0 immunotherapy study testing an ADAM-12-targeted vaccine in cats with confirmed sarcoma when surgery or radiotherapy is no longer possible. Vaccinated cats receive two doses on days 0 and 7 with CT and biopsy follow-up; safety is the primary endpoint and antitumor activity is exploratory.

upsert.title: Radiotherapy plus temozolomide and lomustine for canine high-grade glioma
upsert.summary: Placebo-controlled clinical trial for biopsy-confirmed aggressive glioma. All dogs receive radiotherapy; half additionally receive temozolomide plus lomustine and half placebo. Brain biopsy, chemotherapy and laboratory testing are free and radiotherapy is discounted.

upsert.title: Fluorescence-guided surgery for soft tissue sarcoma
upsert.summary: Clinical surgical study using intraoperative fluorescent dyes to improve visualization of soft tissue sarcoma margins and support more complete tumor removal in dogs and cats.
